questions.question: How many unused PTO days can an employee carry into next year?
questions.reference_answer: Up to five unused PTO days.
questions.reviewer_note: Direct lookup of the carryover limit.

retrieved_evidence.text: Employees may carry over up to five unused PTO days into the next calendar year. Additional unused days expire on December 31.

questions.question: How much PTO does a full-time employee accrue each month?
questions.reference_answer: 1.5 days after each completed month.
questions.reviewer_note: Direct lookup of the monthly accrual rate.

retrieved_evidence.text: Full-time employees accrue 1.5 days of paid time off at the end of each completed month. Part-time employees accrue time proportionally.

questions.question: How much notice is required for planned PTO?
questions.reference_answer: At least two business days plus manager approval.
questions.reviewer_note: Direct lookup of the planned-leave notice rule.

retrieved_evidence.text: Planned PTO requests require at least two business days of notice and manager approval. Unexpected illness should be reported as soon as practical.

questions.question: When does an employee become eligible for scheduled remote work?
questions.reference_answer: After 90 days of employment with manager approval.
questions.reviewer_note: Direct lookup of the eligibility period.

retrieved_evidence.text: Employees become eligible for scheduled remote work after 90 days of employment with manager approval. Remote work is not leave and employees keep their normal working hours.

questions.question: Where may an employee perform remote work?
questions.reference_answer: From the approved home state unless People Operations approves another state in writing.

retrieved_evidence.text: Remote work must take place from the employee's approved home state. Working temporarily from another state requires written approval from People Operations before travel.

questions.question: What is the maximum home-office stipend?
questions.reference_answer: Up to $500 once.
